notes.headline: Photonics Deep Supply Chain (Sancet thesis) — SIVE/LPK/AAOI/IQE: chokepoint holders in the $14B→$154B optical supercycle, multi-year asymmetric holds.
notes.body:
Four chokepoint positions in the photonics value chain:

1. SIVE — CW laser supplier for CPO + 1.6T/3.2T pluggable transceivers. Qualified with JBL, Ayar, Lightmatter, Lightelligence, POET, MRVL Celestial, AMD. Vertical integration path: lasers → full ELS → entire pluggable transceiver → laser fabs/substrates (COHR model). Risk: TAM capture rate, Win Semi volume ramp dependency.

2. LPK — Purest glass substrate equipment exposure (~80% global share). 'ASML of glass substrates.' $650M MC vs $100-200M revenue potential per customer ramp. INTC + Samsung adopting. Equipment cycle risk but asymmetric at current MC.

3. AAOI — Made-in-America photonics supply chain (CW laser fab + 800G/1.6T assembly). Only domestic full-chain alternative to Innolight/Eoptolink/FN. Sovereign DC + onshoring demand. Targeting $400M+/mo revenue H2 2026. Near-term overhang: $600M dilution.

4. IQE — Critical Western epiwafer supplier. MTSI paid off IQE debt because upstream failure would cascade billions downstream. Financially messy but strategically irreplaceable. Point72 position.

Key insight: These are venture-style public equities — correct supply chain calls but financially early-stage. Won't pass momentum filters until revenue inflects. AAOI closest to tradability on swing timeframe. Photonics TAM $14B→$154B in 2 years (Goldman), architecture of choice by NVDA. Not going away.

notes.headline: HBM4 Memory Supercycle Sleepers — VECO/PLAB/ADEA/ACLS/FORM/ONTO/AMKR/RMBS/MKSI: small-cap picks-and-shovels market hasn't priced in yet.

laser_anneal.label: Laser Annealing
laser_anneal.thesis: Veeco laser annealing tools are critical for HBM4 junction formation. Sub-$2.5B mcap means minimal institutional ownership; any NVDA or MU HBM ramp commentary moves VECO disproportionately. Stealth picks-and-shovels.

photomask.label: Lithography Photomask
photomask.thesis: Photronics makes the photomasks used in every lithography step of HBM4 production. Pure commodity-of-process play — every new memory node needs new masks. $2.1B mcap with direct HBM exposure.

hybrid_bonding.label: Hybrid Bonding IP / Tooling
hybrid_bonding.thesis: Adeia holds critical semiconductor IP for hybrid bonding — the stacking technology used in HBM4. IP licensing means high-margin, non-capital-intensive revenue that compounds with every HBM unit shipped. $2.18B mcap severely undervalued relative to RMBS ($13.5B) for comparable IP moat.

ion_implantation.label: Ion Implantation
ion_implantation.thesis: Axcelis ion implantation tools are used in DRAM and HBM doping steps. $2.9B mcap despite being the only independent pure-play ion implant company (Applied and Lam are diversified). Cyclical but deeply levered to HBM capex.

hbm_wafer_test.label: HBM Wafer Testing
hbm_wafer_test.thesis: FormFactor probe cards are the primary test infrastructure for HBM wafers. $6.4B mcap with record HBM demand confirmed (Q1 2026 beat). Every HBM wafer must be tested before stacking — FORM is the gating step that can't be skipped. Already confirmed in FORM Q1 earnings: record HBM demand, record gross margins (49%).

packaging_metrology.label: Advanced Packaging Metrology
packaging_metrology.thesis: Onto Innovation provides critical process control and metrology for HBM advanced packaging. As HBM stacks increase (HBM4 = 16-high stacks), yield management becomes the gating cost factor — ONTO's tools are mandatory. $10.6B mcap, already confirmed in our viav-form thesis.

advanced_packaging_osat.label: Advanced Packaging / OSAT
advanced_packaging_osat.thesis: Amkor is the largest US-listed OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test). Directly assembles and packages HBM stacks for SK Hynix and Samsung. $13.1B mcap with direct HBM revenue exposure. Often overlooked because it's assembly not design, but OSAT is the physical bottleneck in advanced packaging.

memory_ip.label: Memory Interface IP
memory_ip.thesis: Rambus licenses memory interface IP — DDR5, HBM controller IP, and security IP. Every HBM controller must license Rambus IP or fight an infringement lawsuit. $13.5B mcap with royalty revenue that scales with memory unit volume, not capital intensity.

laser_subsystems.label: Laser / Photonics Subsystems
laser_subsystems.thesis: MKS Instruments provides laser subsystems, power delivery, and process control used in HBM wafer processing. $14.9B mcap diversified across semi/industrial/photonics. Less pure-play than FORM/VECO but captures HBM capex across multiple process steps.

indirect_beneficiaries.label: Indirect / Adjacency
indirect_beneficiaries.thesis: Semtech (SMTC) provides signal integrity ICs used in high-speed memory interfaces. MACOM (MTSI) makes RF/microwave components used in test systems and optical interconnects adjacent to HBM packaging. Both benefit from HBM ecosystem buildout indirectly.

lead_lag.horizon: HBM4 production ramp 2026-2028; multi-year capex cycle
lead_lag.chain_flow: MU/SK Hynix HBM capex commitment → FORM wafer test → ONTO metrology → AMKR packaging → VECO/ACLS/PLAB process tools → RMBS/ADEA IP royalties compound per unit

notes.thesis: The HBM4 supercycle picks-and-shovels layer is dominated by small-cap names that have minimal institutional coverage relative to their direct exposure. MU and SK Hynix HBM capex flows directly to this chain. FORM and ONTO already confirmed in Q1 2026 earnings (record HBM demand). ADEA (hybrid bonding IP) and RMBS (memory interface IP) are pure royalty compounders — every HBM unit shipped pays them. VECO/PLAB/ACLS are process-tool sleepers at sub-$3B mcap. AMKR is the OSAT bottleneck — physically assembles the stacks.
caveats: Small caps have wider bid/ask and less liquidity — size accordingly.
HBM cycle could peak if NVDA demand disappoints — all names correlate down sharply.
ADEA's IP position is hybrid bonding specific; if die-to-wafer bonding (alternative) scales, royalty base narrows.
AMKR has significant Samsung/Hynix customer concentration — any vendor shift is binary.
PLAB is purely cyclical on mask orders — no moat beyond process-node participation.
red_card_triggers: MU or SK Hynix publicly delays HBM4 capex by >6 months
Alternative bonding technology renders hybrid bonding obsolete before 2028
US export controls expanded to block OSAT activity (AMKR) or advanced packaging tools

lead_lag.horizon: 20-30 year lease durability; 8-9% dividend yields provide downside

Power interconnection queue delays could push out new builds (5+ years in PJM).

notes.headline: Cooling/Thermal Layer — VRT, MOD: liquid cooling adoption driving 30-40% CAGR.

liquid_cooling.label: Direct Liquid Cooling (DLC)
liquid_cooling.thesis: VRT pure-play DLC leader, NVIDIA GB200 co-design, 3+ year backlog. MOD data center cooling fiscal Q3 +31% sequential, expects $400M+ quarterly, 50-70% growth over next 2 years. SMCI's 70% DLC market share drives this.

air_handling.label: Specialized Air Handling
air_handling.thesis: Specialized HVAC for data center thermal. Less direct AI exposure but real-estate adjacency.

diversified_hvac.label: Diversified Building / HVAC
diversified_hvac.thesis: Johnson Controls — building efficiency. AI is minor revenue contributor; broader cyclical name.

lead_lag.horizon: 3-5 years as DLC adoption ramps from <10% to 50%+ of new DC builds
lead_lag.chain_flow: GPU rack power density (130kW+) → air cooling fails → DLC mandatory → VRT/MOD orderbook

notes.thesis: Liquid cooling adoption is forced by GPU thermal density. SMCI 70% DLC share validates the inflection. MOD's 50-70% growth guidance reflects supply-demand inversion — water scarcity in California/Texas is accelerating adoption further.
caveats: MOD is a small/mid cap with higher vol than VRT.
Hyperscalers may bring some cooling in-house long-term.
Water scarcity could ironically slow adoption if regulators restrict water-cooled designs.
red_card_triggers: NVIDIA changes GPU thermal design specification removing liquid cooling requirement
Major hyperscaler (>20% of VRT revenue) switches to competing cooling vendor
VRT misses revenue guidance by >10% in 2 consecutive quarters

notes.headline: Copper Supercycle — FCX, SCCO: structural 2026-2040 demand from AI DCs + EVs + grid.

majors.label: Copper Majors
majors.thesis: FCX +40% YoY, Grasberg restoration 2027+, largest liquid copper play. SCCO 2026 revenue target $16B (+17%), record 2025 $13.42B. Spot $14.5K/tonne early 2026, consensus $20K+ by 2028-2029.

polymetallic.label: Polymetallic / Hedged
polymetallic.thesis: TECK copper+zinc+coal Chilean expansion. ERO high-grade Brazilian operations, lower permitting risk.

lead_lag.horizon: 10-15 year supercycle; 5% major deposits last decade; 15-17 year permitting lead time
lead_lag.chain_flow: AI DC (50K tonnes/facility) + EV adoption + grid expansion → 50% demand growth → supply-constrained → spot $14.5K → $20K+

notes.thesis: Copper is the single most underappreciated AI-adjacent supercycle. Each AI data center consumes 50,000 tonnes of copper. Combined with EV and grid expansion, demand grows 50% by 2030. Supply is structurally constrained — only 5% of major deposits discovered in the last decade, 15-17 year permitting lead times.
caveats: Cyclical macro exposure — global recession would dent demand near-term despite structural setup.
Grasberg/Chilean political risk (resource nationalism).
Copper trades on China sentiment — any Chinese stimulus disappointment hits the basket.
red_card_triggers: Global recession confirmed (PMI <45 for 3+ months across US/EU/China simultaneously)
Large new copper mine supply comes online >12 months ahead of schedule
Aluminum achieves cost and conductivity parity for EV wiring at production scale

notes.headline: Defense Supercycle — LMT, RTX, NOC + drones: $526B combined backlog, AI/autonomous +15% YoY.

primes.label: Defense Primes
primes.thesis: LMT $179B record backlog, F-35 stabilized. RTX $251B order book — largest in defense. NOC $96B record backlog, naval + electronic warfare. Combined backlog $526B = 3+ years revenue visibility.

drones_autonomy.label: Drones & Autonomous Systems
drones_autonomy.thesis: AVAV drone leader, Ukraine validated. KTOS defense automation + satellite/autonomous platforms. AI/autonomous segment growing 15%+ YoY vs <5% for legacy platforms.

naval_land.label: Naval / Land Systems
naval_land.thesis: Submarines, armored vehicles, combat systems integrating AI. More cyclical than primes.

space_isr.label: Space ISR / Dual-Use Intelligence
space_isr.thesis: BlackSky (BKSY) and Spire Global (SPIR) represent the commercial space intelligence layer that DoD is actively scaling as a cost-efficient alternative to classified satellite programs. BKSY operates a constellation of high-revisit optical satellites — tasked by DoD/NGA for real-time ISR. SPIR provides RF/weather data from 100+ LEO satellites. Both operate on recurring government contracts and benefit directly from the Defense Supercycle: defense ISR budgets growing with autonomous battlefield awareness demand, and Ukraine proving the operational value of commercial satellite intelligence. Fastest-growing segment within defense ISR — higher beta than primes, episodic move potential on contract wins.

lead_lag.horizon: 5-10 year defense cycle; bipartisan support guarantees budget through 2030
lead_lag.chain_flow: Geopolitical escalation → bipartisan budget support → backlog accumulation → autonomous/AI segment + space ISR outgrow legacy platforms

notes.thesis: Defense TAM $1T+ locked in with bipartisan support. Taiwan tensions and Ukraine validation drive autonomous systems specifically. Backlogs of $526B combined for the primes provide unprecedented visibility. AVAV/KTOS represent the AI-defense intersection growing fastest.
caveats: Political risk if defense spending becomes a budget cut target.
Primes are slow-growth (single-digit revenue) but high-quality. Multiple compression possible.
Drone names (AVAV) trade on news flow — high vol.
Supply chain bottlenecks (semis for guidance, rare earths for magnets) create execution risk.

US defense budget cut >10% in a single fiscal year via Congressional reconciliation
Primary program cancellation for LMT F-35 or RTX Patriot/LTAMDS at scale

notes.headline: Macro Supercycle Context — $725B hyperscaler capex (+77%), 1.2% US GDP, electrification 1920s analogue.

hyperscaler_capex_2026.comparison: Exceeds telecom buildout (1.0% GDP), trails railroad (6.0% GDP)

historical_analogies.railroads_1880s: Infrastructure phase 2024-2026 = railroad buildout. Consolidation/bankruptcy phase 2028-2035. Equipment suppliers (AMAT, ETN, VRT) win mid-term; operators (hyperscalers) win 50-yr long-term. Many stranded assets become essential decades later.
historical_analogies.electrification_1920s: Closest current analogue. Grid buildout 1920s = power infrastructure 2024-2026. Excess capacity risk 2026-2027. Resolution 1950s = AI productivity boom 2035-2040 justifies capex. Suppliers durability HIGH; capex cycle longer than railroads.
historical_analogies.fiber_telecom_late_1990s: Fiber overbuild 2000-2001 = DC capex 2024-2026 risk parallel. Stranded assets (Global Crossing) became essential broadband decades later. Equipment winners (CIENA, JDSU) > carriers (bankruptcy). For AI: AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/ASML/ETN > hyperscaler operators in 2028+ margin compression scenarios.
historical_analogies.china_commodity_2000s: Urbanization 2000s = AI infrastructure 2026-2030. Commodities then: iron ore/steel/coal/oil. Now: copper/lithium/nickel/uranium. Supply winners durable 8-12 years. Spot copper $14.5K → $20K+ consensus 2028-2029.

notes.thesis: We are in Phase 2 of an AI-driven supercycle most closely analogous to electrification of the 1920s. Hyperscaler capex of $725B (+77% YoY) at 1.2% of US GDP is unprecedented in modern history outside of WWII mobilization. Equipment suppliers and bottleneck-node owners (HBM, optics, power, cooling) carry the highest-quality earnings visibility through 2028. Hyperscalers themselves face a capex-to-revenue conversion risk by 2028-2029 if AI monetization disappoints.
key_signals_to_watch: Quarterly hyperscaler capex guidance — any cut = supercycle topping signal
NVDA forward gross margin trajectory — compression = ASIC competition real
HBM ASP trends in MU earnings — declining = supply catching up
Sovereign AI deal announcements — pipeline of $300B+ over 2026-2030
Power interconnection queue clearing — bottleneck for entire chain
caveats: Capex-to-revenue gap is the existential question. Closing it = supercycle extends. Failing = 2028 cliff.
Historical analogies all show 30-50% drawdowns mid-cycle even when long-term thesis was correct.
Geopolitical disruption (Taiwan, US-China decoupling) could fragment the global supply chain rapidly.
Open-source models (LLAMA, etc.) commoditize the model layer — winners shift from creators to deployers.
red_card_triggers: 2+ hyperscalers simultaneously announce AI capex pause in earnings calls
Fed pivots to rate hikes (>2 consecutive 25bp increases) compressing growth multiples
Generational valuation compression event (AI P/E de-rating >30% from peak)

notes.headline: Server/Rack Integration Layer — SMCI, DELL, ANET: the missing layer between chip and cloud that assembles the actual racks.
notes.thesis: Between chip (NVDA/AVGO) and cloud (hyperscalers) sits the rack integration layer. Arista (ANET) is the Tier 1 switching fabric play — its 400G/800G Ethernet switches are in every major AI cluster. DELL is the OEM beneficiary with PowerEdge GPU servers. SMCI (Super Micro) is the pure-play liquid-cooled server design house — closest to the AI rack build — but has had accounting/audit issues (10-K delays, Hindenburg short report). SMCI is only tradeable once accounting credibility is restored. ANET is the cleanest name: recurring software (EOS), hyperscaler stickiness, no controversy.

lead_lag.horizon: 1-2 years alongside the rack buildout cycle
lead_lag.rationale: ANET leads because networking infrastructure gets ordered before servers ship. DELL lags because server OEM margins are thin and timing is lumpy. SMCI is uninvestable until audit completion.

caveats: SMCI: do not size until FY2024 10-K is filed and auditor concern resolved. Prior Hindenburg allegations of accounting irregularities.
ANET valuation is rich — trades at premium to software comps on hardware revenue. Multiple compression risk if hyperscaler capex guidance disappoints.
DELL has PC/commercial business drag — only ~20% of revenue is ISG (AI servers). Blended multiple stays depressed.
red_card_triggers: ANET loses >1 major hyperscaler spine-leaf contract to Cisco or Nokia
Merchant silicon displaces ANET's networking stack in next-gen AI cluster design
AI cluster architecture shifts to flat topology or InfiniBand dominance, removing Ethernet switching layer

notes.headline: Nuclear Power for AI — CEG/CCJ/NNE: hyperscalers are signing 15-20yr PPAs, Three Mile Island Unit 1 is operational, Calpine acquisition adds 26GW contracted generation.

lead_lag.horizon: 1-3 years for existing fleet PPAs; 5-10 years for SMR construction
lead_lag.rationale: CEG leads because it has existing operational capacity and signed contracts — no construction risk. CCJ leads the uranium supply cycle by 2-3 years ahead of SMR builds. NNE/OKLO/SMR lag by years — revenue is post-2028 at earliest.

existing_fleet_ppa.label: Existing Fleet + Long-Term PPAs
contracts: Calpine acquisition: adds 26GW natural gas + hydro contracted generation
existing_fleet_ppa.thesis: CEG is the only investment-grade vehicle to capture AI power demand NOW. Existing reactors produce power at $25-35/MWh all-in cost; hyperscalers pay $100-130/MWh via PPA — 3-5x spread locks in 40-50% margins on contracted load. The Calpine acquisition (closed Q1 2026) makes CEG the largest US competitive power generator — 26GW additional capacity broadens the contract base beyond nuclear. FY27E EPS $13.51 (+16% YoY). Analyst avg PT $380 = +28% from $298 current. This is a Koss-quality position: contracted cash flows, irreplaceable asset base, CEO execution, pricing power asymmetry.

uranium_supply.label: Uranium Supply Chain
uranium_supply.thesis: Cameco (CCJ) is the blue-chip uranium supply proxy — Tier 1 mines in Saskatchewan (Cigar Lake, McArthur River). Any new nuclear PPA or SMR contract announcement triggers a 2-3yr forward demand signal for uranium fuel. UUUU (Energy Fuels) is strategically important as a domestic US uranium producer — Russia import ban makes US supply chain critical. Size CCJ at half vs CEG: longer lag, more volatile, geopolitical risk from Kazakhstan/Russia.

smr_options.label: SMR Pure-Plays (5-10yr options)
smr_options.thesis: NuScale (NNE) is furthest along in NRC licensing for small modular reactors. Oklo (OKLO) is Sam Altman-backed, targeting DOE approvals 2027-2028. These are long-duration options: no revenue now, narrative-driven, 50-80% drawdowns possible. Do NOT size like CEG — these are lottery tickets on the 2030 nuclear future, not contracted cash flows.

power_infrastructure.label: Power Infrastructure (indirect beneficiaries)
power_infrastructure.thesis: Eaton (ETN) and GE Vernova (GEV) benefit from the power infrastructure buildout surrounding nuclear and data centers: transformers, switchgear, grid interconnect equipment. These are derivative plays — they benefit whether the power source is nuclear, gas, or solar.

notes.thesis: Nuclear is the only 24/7 carbon-free baseload solution that can satisfy AI data center power demand at scale. The thesis has moved from speculative to contractual: Microsoft restarted Three Mile Island Unit 1 under a 20-year PPA; Google signed a 500MW nuclear PPA with Constellation; Amazon's AWS has signed multiple 15-year agreements. CEG's Calpine acquisition (closed 2026) added ~26GW of contracted generation, transforming CEG into the largest competitive power generator in the US. The economics are compelling: hyperscalers are paying $100–130/MWh for 24/7 carbon-free power — 3-5x the merchant spot rate — because data center uptime is non-negotiable. CEG's contracted revenue base now offers utility-like earnings visibility with tech-sector pricing power. CCJ (Cameco) is the uranium supply proxy — 2-3 year lag from contract to fuel delivery. notes.headline: AI Inference & Edge Layer — ARM, QCOM, NVDA Jetson: as AI shifts from training to inference, the chip mix and winners change.
notes.thesis: The AI buildout has two phases: training (build the model — needs massive GPU clusters, NVDA's core market) and inference (run the model — broader architecture competition). Inference is growing faster than training spend, and the optimal chip for inference is NOT always a GPU. ARM architecture dominates inference at the edge — every smartphone, every laptop, every IoT device runs ARM. QCOM's Snapdragon X Elite with NPU is the PC inference play. Apple Silicon (M4/A18) is the gold standard for on-device inference but AAPL doesn't sell the chip. The inflection: as inference moves to the edge (on-device, not cloud), NVDA's share of inference workloads is threatened. This is a 2-3 year transition, not immediate.

lead_lag.horizon: 2-3 years for on-device inference to become a meaningful workload shift
lead_lag.rationale: ARM licenses its architecture to everyone — every inference chip (QCOM, Apple, MediaTek, Ampere cloud) runs ARM ISA. ARM royalties compound as inference scales. QCOM is the most direct AI PC/edge pure-play. NVDA's inference exposure is primarily data center inference (NIM microservices on H100/B200) — not edge.

architecture_map.edge_inference: ARM Cortex-X / Neoverse, QCOM Snapdragon NPU, Apple ANE

caveats: ARM trades at 70-80x forward earnings — enormous multiple. Any inference growth slowdown or NVDA competition is punishing.
QCOM has a smartphone cyclical overhang — AI PC momentum needs to outrun handset weakness.
NVDA is not standing still — Grace Blackwell (CPU+GPU) and Jetson Orin target edge inference directly.
On-device inference is primarily a consumer story — different catalysts than enterprise AI capex cycle.

notes.headline: Photonics start-to-finish: bottlenecks are NOT raw materials — they're conversion, assembly, and test (low-fungibility, high-yield-curve steps)

supply_chain_steps.name: Mining / smelting / refining (indium)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: BYPRODUCT COUPLING — indium recovered from zinc residues, not primary mining; many zinc producers lack indium circuits. China refines ~68% of global primary indium. Geopolitical/policy choke point at refining stage.
supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: Geological abundance high; industrial recovery + purification is the limit. Optical-grade purity adds another tier.

supply_chain_steps.name: InP substrate (crystal growth + wafering)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: WAFER-SIZE GAP vs Si CMOS. Historical 2-4 inch; transition to 6-inch is a multi-year qualification across the entire downstream stack (epi susceptors, lithography chucks, dicing). Brittleness + warp/TTV control.

tickers.role: 6-inch InP scalable wafer fab announced (laser sources for AI transceivers)

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: Sumitomo Electric (5802.T) is the dominant InP substrate maker — not US-listed.

supply_chain_steps.name: Epitaxial growth (MOCVD / MBE)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: ATOMIC-SCALE PROCESS IP — proprietary recipes, specialized tooling, hazardous precursor chemistries. Low fungibility; concentrated among captive fabs + a few specialty epi houses.

tickers.role: nLight — GaAs/InP semiconductor laser fab + fiber laser specialist; high-power laser sources for industrial/defense + datacom diode pumps
tickers.exposure: DIRECT pure-play on semiconductor laser sources (smaller scale than COHR/LITE but cleanest exposure to laser-diode demand ramp)

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: IQE plc (IQE.L) is the dominant external epi house but London-listed.

supply_chain_steps.name: Wafer fabrication (photonics front+back end)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: PROCESS COMPLEXITY — InP PIC flow can involve 243+ steps. Sidewall roughness, etch-depth precision, gold metallization (NOT shareable with Si CMOS lines). Defect density drives yield = cost-per-good-die.
supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: InP fab yields historically lag silicon CMOS — disclosed indirectly via gross margin trends.

supply_chain_steps.name: Dicing, test, yield
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: TEST THROUGHPUT — optical test slower than CMOS electrical probing (fiber alignment + power measurement). InP brittleness raises edge-defect risk. Test capacity gates shipments during demand surges.

tickers.role: Optical burn-in test systems (FOX-NP for photonic ICs)
Plasma etch chemistry, vacuum, photonics process control

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: AEHR is the most levered to AI-photonics test specifically (FOX-NP for VCSEL/PIC burn-in).

supply_chain_steps.name: Component assembly + hermetic packaging
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: PRECISION ALIGNMENT — single-mode fiber requires <1 µm tolerance with active alignment under live optical monitoring. Hermetic sealing (laser welding, He leak test) is throughput-limited. Hermetic package/Kovar/feedthrough supply gates final shipment AFTER most cost is incurred.

tickers.role: Fabrinet — contract manufacturer for optical assembly + hermetic packaging at scale
tickers.exposure: DIRECT — captures per-unit assembly fee for most major OEMs (COHR/LITE/CIEN/NVDA optical engines)

tickers.role: Jabil — high-volume electronics + optical module assembly

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: Hermetic ceramic/Kovar housing supply is a hidden choke point — niche specialty suppliers, not publicly tracked.

supply_chain_steps.name: Transceiver module (optics + high-speed electronics)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: SYSTEM TEST + DSP integration — coherent test time + multi-temperature calibration. Module test capacity gates shipments even when die supply exists.
supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: Coherent (COHR) is the broadest single bet — substrates + epi + PIC + module all in-house.

supply_chain_steps.name: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: RELOCATION OF BOTTLENECKS — optical engines move into the same package as switch ASIC/GPU. Yield coupling: an optical fail scraps an expensive electronic package. Test access constrained, fiber attach must survive reflow profiles. Bottleneck migrates from module final test → wafer-level/package-level test + fiber attach.

tickers.role: Silicon photonics foundry for CPO partners
Switch ASIC + co-packaged optics (Tomahawk 5/6 + CPO variants)
Spectrum-X/NVLink CPO roadmap (silicon photonics inside switches)
Wafer-level optics (WLO) — micro-lens arrays + assembly tech for CPO fiber coupling; ALSO automotive DDIC, AR LCoS microdisplays. WLO is small % of rev (~5-10%); main business is display driver ICs.
tickers.exposure: INDIRECT — WLO is real CPO-adjacent tech but represents <10% of HIMX revenue. Equity moves on automotive DDIC + AI compute, not optical. Watch as CALL OPTION, not pure-play.

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: CPO doesn't shrink the supply chain — it shifts where the value/risk concentrates (advanced packaging, test, fiber attach).

supply_chain_steps.name: Fiber + connector deployment
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: FIBER PURITY + CONNECTOR PRECISION — preforms with ppb impurity levels, draw control. Single-mode fiber MFD ~9 µm with attenuation targets ≤0.4 dB/km. Connectorization, ferrule polishing, cleaning regimes scale with rack/row fiber count.

tickers.role: Corning — dominant single-mode fiber maker + bare fiber + connectors

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: AI rack architecture (GPU-scale fabrics) raises fiber count per rack — shifts value to bulk fiber/jumper supply.

highest_margin_choke_points: Test capacity (AEHR / COHU / CAMT / ONTO / KEYS) — gates shipments, hard to scale fast
Hermetic packaging + alignment (FN as the scale player) — late-stage gate, high inventory cost if blocked

Vertically integrated photonics (COHR) — captures end-to-end value from substrate to module

structural_winners: FN (Fabrinet) — every transceiver assembled at scale passes through them; pricing power as bottleneck
COHR — only US-listed name with substrate + epi + PIC + module all in-house
AEHR — only pure-play optical burn-in test maker; AI photonics ramp = direct revenue
GLW — fiber demand scales with rack fiber count; AI cluster builds raise per-rack fiber count materially
structural_risks: AAOI / pluggable specialists — CPO long-term threatens pluggable TAM
Pure-play silicon photonics (POET) — execution risk if heterogeneous integration timeline slips
Indium price-spike risk → all InP-dependent margins compress in unison

lead_lag.rationale: Hyperscaler/integrator capex commitments (per linked notes) flow downstream through multi-year photonics ramps. Substrate scaling alone is a 2-4 year cycle. Photonics suppliers benefit on a 1-4Q lag from each capex commitment milestone.

notes.headline: AI infra state of play: Energy = primary conviction · copper-to-optics = highest-conviction networking · Memory = secular not cyclical

subtheses.title: AI Energy is the primary conviction play
subtheses.argument: Power is THE defining constraint of the AI buildout, not compute. Hyperscalers acknowledged 'power-and-compute constrained' in unison; compute side has visible relief paths (CoWoS expansion, foundry capex, custom silicon). Power side is structurally bounded by permitting + interconnect + grid construction cycles measured in YEARS not quarters. Allocations rotating beyond accelerators/networking into the energy stack.
trade_setup: BE — on-site fuel cells bypass interconnect queue; relief-valve trade with shorter timeline than IPP/nuclear
GEV — grid equipment (transformers, switchgear) front-runs IPP capex
VRT — datacenter cooling + power conditioning; structural beneficiary of high-density AI racks
IREN — 'power-secured site' compute play (neocloud overlap with energy thesis — they own the substations)
subtheses.extension_note: Reframes the prior 'EARLY cycle phase' read on Power as structurally MORE important than compute — not just earlier in the cycle but a bigger pool of capital.

subtheses.title: Copper-to-optics is the highest-conviction networking theme
subtheses.argument: At 800G+ lane rates, copper interconnect loss + retiming complexity hits a wall. Silicon photonics, EML (externally modulated laser) lasers, and co-packaged optics are the only path forward. Most investors can't name the names — that's where the alpha is. Multi-year transition because every hyperscaler design needs to qualify the new optical engines.
speculative_picks: SIVE-B.ST (Sivers Semiconductors) — Stockholm-listed silicon-photonics alpha, see sive-apple-silicon-photonics note
IQE.L (IQE plc) — London-listed dominant external epi house for compound semis; not US-tradeable but strategically critical
subtheses.extension_note: Sharpens the prior photonics thesis: the COPPER → OPTICS transition itself is the alpha, not just the test/inspection bottleneck. EML lasers + silicon photonics are the secular shift.

subtheses.title: AI Memory is no longer cyclical — it's secular
subtheses.argument: Samsung disclosed 2027 demand pre-booked. SNDK Q3 print: 78% GM, $11B in customer financial guarantees. Today's signal: supply constrained through 2028 (extending Samsung's 2027 read by another year). Demand accelerating faster than any model projected. The historical NAND/DRAM cycle (peak → reversion → trough → recovery) is broken because AI inference creates a permanent floor on demand that doesn't unwind on a price reset.
subtheses.extension_note: Updates the horizon from 'multi-year' to 'through 2028.' The structural reframing matters for valuation — secular memory deserves a tech-platform multiple, not a cyclical commodity multiple. MU/SNDK should re-rate higher when the market accepts this.

trade_setup_summary: REWEIGHT: shift conviction from compute-side (NVDA/AVGO/etc) toward energy-side (BE/GEV/VRT/IREN). Compute has relief paths; power is structurally bounded.
ADD: photonics secular winners (LITE/AAOI/COHR/FN/AEHR) on copper→optics transition. Sub-bench: POET/TSEM/MTSI as architectural alpha.
EXTEND HOLD: memory cohort (MU/SNDK) into 2027-2028. Don't trim on cycle-peak fears — the cycle is broken.
WATCH: SIVE (foreign) for silicon photonics confirmation; signs of widespread CPO adoption in 2026 H2.

Copper-to-optics kill: CPO timeline slips by 12+ months (qualification or yield issues). AAOI most exposed if pluggable TAM compresses faster than expected.
Memory secular kill: hyperscaler concentration risk — $11B in SNDK guarantees from 3-5 customers. Bilateral risk.
All three theses share a common kill: AI infrastructure capex revision down.

notes.headline: Glass Substrate Value Chain — GLW/LRCX/ONTO/KLAC + Japanese specialists: AI packaging next frontier.

glass_materials.label: Glass Materials
glass_materials.thesis: Corning (GLW) is the dominant US player in specialty glass — borosilicate glass for substrates is a natural extension of their Display and Optical Physics segments. ASGLY (Asahi Glass / AGC, 5201.T) and NIDGY (Nippon Electric Glass, 5214.T) are the Japanese incumbents already supplying prototype glass panels to Intel, AMD, and TSMC packaging lines. Glass substrates offer 50% lower signal loss, 40% better flatness, and near-zero moisture absorption vs organic — enabling denser interconnect pitch at scale.

tgv_equipment.label: TGV Equipment (Through-Glass Via)
tgv_equipment.thesis: Lpkf Laser (LPK) makes the laser systems that drill Through-Glass Vias — the critical enabling step that allows vertical signal routing through glass panels. No TGV drilling = no glass substrate chip integration. LPKF is the pick-and-shovel play with the most direct exposure; their LIDE (Laser Induced Deep Etching) process is the leading TGV formation technology.

etching_systems.label: Etching & Patterning
etching_systems.thesis: Lam Research (LRCX) etching systems are required to pattern the fine-pitch redistribution layers on glass panels. Glass etching has tighter process windows than organic — favorable for Lam's high-selectivity etch tools. Incremental TAM expansion as glass substrate adoption scales into HVM.

dicing_equipment.label: Dicing Equipment
dicing_equipment.thesis: Disco Corp (DSCSY, 6146.T) is the world leader in dicing/grinding equipment. Glass panels are harder and more brittle than organic substrates — Disco's stealth dicing laser technology is the preferred singulation method. Direct beneficiary of glass substrate HVM ramp.

bonding_systems.label: Bonding Systems
bonding_systems.thesis: Shibaura Mechatronics (SMHSF) supplies precision bonding equipment used in the chip-to-glass attach process. Glass substrate's coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch with silicon requires tighter bonding tolerances — plays to Shibaura's high-precision equipment strengths.

inspection_tools.label: Inspection & Metrology
inspection_tools.thesis: Onto Innovation (ONTO) and KLA (KLAC) provide the inspection and metrology systems required to qualify glass substrate lines. Glass introduces new defect modes (micro-cracks, via sidewall roughness, CTE-driven warpage) that require new inspection recipes. Both are already name-dropped by substrate players as key qualification partners. ONTO is the higher-beta play; KLAC has the broadest moat across all inspection nodes.

notes.headline: Semiconductor AI Supercycle Full Stack — 10-layer playbook: Memory/Optical/Power/Equipment/Edge to AI Infra.

memory.label: 1 — Memory (HBM / NAND / DRAM)
memory.thesis: HBM4 = the new oil. Not a commodity anymore — strategic infrastructure. MU is the only US HBM manufacturer, shipping HBM3E to NVDA, AMD, and hyperscalers. WDC/STX/SNDK capture NAND/HDD cold storage for AI training archives. AMAT and LRCX are the equipment picks-and-shovels for HBM stack deposition and etch. The memory supercycle is driven by AI training and inference workload growth — not the PC/smartphone cycle of the past.

controllers.label: 2 — Controllers
controllers.thesis: The traffic cops of every AI system. Overlooked, undervalued, critical. RMBS: memory interface chips (DDR5, HBM controllers). SIMO: mixed-signal controllers for storage. ATOM: atomic/timing controllers for AI racks. MCHP: microcontrollers everywhere AI touches industrial. ADI and TXN: analog/mixed-signal workhorses — every power rail, sensor interface, and data converter in AI infra runs through them. Secular growth with lower volatility than pure-play AI names.

packaging_testing.label: 3 — Packaging & Testing (CoWoS / Chiplets)
packaging_testing.thesis: CoWoS. HBM stacking. Chiplets. This is where chips become systems. AMKR is the largest advanced packaging OSAT — primary beneficiary of TSMC's CoWoS capacity expansion. ONTO and CAMT provide inspection/metrology for advanced packaging nodes. FORM and ACMR supply the equipment for wafer cleaning and advanced substrate processing. COHU handles test handler equipment. The entire AI chip supply chain routes through this layer — no advanced packaging = no HBM-attached GPU.

next_gen_memory.label: 4 — Next-Gen Memory (MRAM / ReRAM / Beyond DRAM)
next_gen_memory.thesis: Beyond DRAM. Early-stage. Asymmetric upside when the cycle arrives. MRAM (Everspin): embedded magnetoresistive RAM for edge/industrial AI. GSIT (GSI Technology): SRAM and AI accelerator memory. NVEC: spintronics R&D play. NLST: LRDIMM patent licensing. CEVA: DSP/NPU IP for on-device AI memory management. Higher risk, earlier stage — position sizing accordingly. Option value on the memory architecture shift that occurs when DRAM scaling hits physical limits.

optical_interconnect.label: 5 — Optical / Interconnect (CPO / 800G→1.6T)
optical_interconnect.thesis: The hottest sub-sector in semis right now. 800G → 1.6T upgrade cycle is underway. CPO (Co-Packaged Optics) is the next arms race — moves optics inside the switch package, eliminating pluggable transceivers. MRVL just paid $5.5B for Celestial AI to own this layer. LITE/AAOI/COHR: transceiver manufacturers. CIEN: optical networking systems. FN: precision fiber connectors. POET/LWLG: silicon photonics foundry capability (national strategic asset framing). MTSI/TSEM: compound semiconductor (GaAs/InP) foundry for optical chips. GLW: specialty fiber and glass for optical cables. Every GPU-to-GPU link in a hyperscaler DC is optical.

edge_ai.label: 6 — Edge AI (Devices / Autos / Factories)
edge_ai.thesis: AI leaves the data center. Devices. Cars. Factories. Multi-year secular trend just getting started. QCOM: Snapdragon X Elite leads on-device AI NPU. CEVA: DSP/NPU IP cores licensed across 200+ chip companies for edge inference. SYNA: touchscreen and display AI integration. INDI: automotive ethernet and in-vehicle networking for AI-enabled vehicles. QUIK (QuickLogic): ultra-low-power edge AI processors. VLN/SMTC: sensor interface ICs for factory and automotive AI. The edge AI TAM is larger than data center AI long-term — it just moves slower.

ai_infra_systems.label: 7 — AI Infra Systems (Full Stack)
ai_infra_systems.thesis: The 'Nvidia-only' era is over. The full stack is getting priced in. NVDA remains the GPU compute anchor. AVGO: custom ASIC (XPU) for Google TPU/Meta MTIA/Apple — the anti-Nvidia trade within AI infra. ARM: CPU IP in every AI chip. MRVL: custom silicon + networking ASICs. CRDO: high-speed SerDes for rack-scale AI interconnect. SGH: specialty memory modules and DRAM for AI servers. SKYT (Skywater): US-based foundry services, increasing national security relevance. The insight: AVGO/MRVL custom silicon business is the most direct hedge against hyperscaler NVDA dependency.

power.label: 8 — Power (DC Power / GaN / SiC)
power.thesis: AI data centers are power monsters. Unsexy. Essential. Increasingly scarce. MPWR: DC-DC converters for GPU power delivery — directly attached to every AI accelerator board. VICR: high-density power modules (48V bus architecture). POWI: power management ICs for data center PSUs. GANX (GaN Systems, now absorbed): GaN power conversion for efficiency gains. AEHR: burn-in test equipment for SiC/GaN power devices. TXN: broad analog/power management presence across all tiers. The power layer gets tighter as every hyperscaler runs out of grid allocation — equipment that extracts more performance per watt wins.

equipment.label: 9 — Equipment (Picks & Shovels Foundation)
equipment.thesis: $133B in equipment sales in 2025. Growing to $145B in 2026. Without these, nothing above gets built. ASML: EUV monopoly — the only company that can make the machines that make the chips. AMAT: broadest equipment portfolio (CVD, PVD, CMP, etch). LRCX: etch and deposition leader. KLAC: inspection and metrology — the quality control layer. ONTO: advanced packaging inspection. ACMR (ACM Research): wet cleaning equipment gaining share in China and leading-edge fabs. Equipment is the most durable layer of the AI supercycle — lead times of 12–18 months mean backlog visibility is exceptional.

future_tech.label: 10 — Future-Tech (Silicon Photonics / Compound Semi)
future_tech.thesis: Silicon photonics foundry capacity = national strategic asset. LWLG (Lightwave Logic): electro-optic polymer modulators — potentially replacing lithium niobate in CPO applications. POET: optical interposer platform (InP on Si). AXTI (AXT): compound semiconductor substrates (InP, GaAs, Ge) — constrained supply for optical and RF chips. TSEM (Tower Semiconductor): analog/mixed-signal foundry with silicon photonics capability. GFS (GlobalFoundries): mature node foundry, defense and auto exposure. IPGP (IPG Photonics): high-power fiber lasers used in semiconductor manufacturing. These names carry the highest speculative premium and require longest holding horizon.

lead_lag.horizon: 2026–2030 AI supercycle; equipment and memory lead, edge AI and future-tech lag by 18–36 months
lead_lag.chain_flow: Power & Cooling → Equipment & Materials → Semiconductors → Connectivity → AI Infrastructure → Software → AI Systems. Design → FAB → Assembly & Packaging → Test → Deployment. The alpha is in mapping the full stack — not just owning the headline GPU name.

notes.thesis: The AI trade is no longer one ticker. It's a full stack. The complete semiconductor playbook maps 10 distinct layers from Power & Cooling to AI Systems — each with its own set of picks-and-shovels beneficiaries. Key insight: the market is sequentially pricing in each layer as supply constraints become visible. Memory (HBM) got priced first. Optical/Interconnect is the hottest sub-sector right now (800G→1.6T, CPO arms race). Packaging/Testing (CoWoS, chiplets) is the supply bottleneck. Power is increasingly scarce and underappreciated. Edge AI is multi-year secular and just getting started. Map the full stack — that's where the alpha is.
caveats: This is a 10-layer framework — position sizing across all layers creates concentration risk in 'AI' as a single macro factor.
Equipment (AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/ASML) is the most durable but has already re-rated significantly — entry timing matters.
Next-gen memory (Layer 4) and future-tech (Layer 10) are early-stage with binary outcome risk.
Edge AI adoption timeline is slower than data center — consumer/auto cycles add uncertainty.
China export controls create asymmetric risk for AMAT, LRCX, KLAC — monitor policy quarterly.
MRVL $5.5B Celestial AI acquisition must integrate successfully for optical layer thesis to compound.
The 'Nvidia-only era is over' claim depends on hyperscaler custom ASIC programs shipping at scale — unproven in volume.

notes.headline: Optical Communications Full Chain — IC Design/Materials/Components/Packaging: CPO + 800G→1.6T arms race.

ic_design_asic.label: IC Design — ASIC & xPU
ic_design_asic.thesis: The ASIC/xPU design layer is where optical capability gets integrated at the chip level. NVDA and MRVL are designing optical DSPs and switch ASICs with embedded photonic interfaces. AVGO's custom ASIC business (Google TPU, Meta MTIA) integrates optical I/O. INTC (Intel) is building CPO into future Xeon and AI accelerators. AMD and CSCO are designing network ASICs that consume optical bandwidth. This is the demand-side anchor — every optical component downstream exists to serve these chips.

ic_design_photonic.label: IC Design — Photonic IC
ic_design_photonic.thesis: Photonic IC design is where silicon photonics and InP-based PICs get architected. MRVL paid $5.5B for Celestial AI specifically to own this layer — electro-optic modulator arrays, photodetectors, and driver ICs co-designed with the switch ASIC. LITE (Lumentum) and COHR (Coherent) design and fab their own photonic ICs for transceivers and CPO modules. This is the fastest-moving design layer as the industry transitions from pluggable to CPO.

wafer_foundry.label: Wafer Foundry (Si Photonics / InP / GaAs)
wafer_foundry.thesis: TSMC (TSM) is the leading silicon photonics foundry — its SiPho process node is used by AVGO, MRVL, and NVDA for integrated photonic ICs. Tower Semiconductor (TSEM) is the analog/mixed-signal foundry with a dedicated silicon photonics platform (acquired from Mellanox/Nvidia). GlobalFoundries (GFS) has a silicon photonics process for datacom applications. UMC serves mature node optical driver ICs. Foundry allocation for silicon photonics is constrained — another supply bottleneck forming.

materials_inp.label: Materials — InP Substrate & Epitaxy
materials_inp.thesis: Indium Phosphide (InP) is the substrate of choice for high-speed EML lasers, photodetectors, and direct-modulation lasers in optical transceivers. AXTI (AXT Inc) is the primary US-listed InP and GaAs substrate supplier — a critical chokepoint in the optical supply chain. IQE supplies InP and GaAs epitaxial wafers (grown layers) that define laser performance. Supply of InP substrates is constrained globally — AXTI is directly in the path of every optical ramp.

materials_fiber_connectors.label: Materials — Optical Fiber / Connectors
materials_fiber_connectors.thesis: Corning (GLW) is the dominant optical fiber manufacturer globally — every datacenter fiber run, MPO trunk cable, and WDM fiber uses Corning glass. Also makes VSFF connectors and MPO connector hardware. Amphenol (APH) supplies MPO connectors and VSFF connectors for high-density patch panels. Both are picks-and-shovels with durable pricing power — fiber and connector demand scales linearly with port count, and port count is exploding with 800G/1.6T upgrades.

laser_vcsel_eml.label: Optical Components — Laser Sources (VCSEL + EML)
laser_vcsel_eml.thesis: The laser is the most critical component in any optical transceiver. Two dominant architectures: VCSEL (lower speed, shorter reach, cheaper — used in AOC and 100G/400G) and EML (higher speed, longer reach, dominant in 800G/1.6T). LITE (Lumentum) and COHR (Coherent) are the top two EML laser suppliers globally. AVGO makes VCSELs for its own transceivers (Apple, hyperscalers). AAOI (Applied Optoelectronics) is a smaller pure-play with high beta. EML supply is constrained for 800G — LITE and COHR benefit most from the 800G→1.6T transition.

optical_module_assembly.label: Optical Components — Module Assembly & Integration
optical_module_assembly.thesis: Optical module assembly integrates lasers, detectors, drivers, and fiber interfaces into pluggable or CPO modules. COHR and LITE are vertically integrated — they make lasers AND assemble modules. CSCO sources modules from the ecosystem and integrates them into switches. MRVL's Celestial AI acquisition brings CPO module integration in-house. FN (Fabrinet) is the contract manufacturer for nearly every optical module brand — LITE, COHR, CSCO, VIAV all outsource production to FN. NOK provides optical networking systems. FN is the most diversified optical picks-and-shovels.

wdm_filter_splitter.label: Optical Components — WDM / Filter / Splitter
wdm_filter_splitter.thesis: Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) multiplexes multiple wavelengths onto one fiber — the key technology enabling 800G/1.6T on existing fiber plant. LITE and COHR make the WDM filter components. CIEN (Ciena) is the systems-level WDM networking leader for carrier and datacenter interconnect. GLW supplies WDM fiber. VIAV (Viavi Solutions) makes optical filters and test instruments for WDM characterization. The WDM layer is both component supply AND network systems — CIEN captures the systems margin.

packaging_testing.label: Packaging & Testing (OSATs + Test Equipment)
packaging_testing.thesis: Optical module packaging requires precision alignment of laser-to-fiber and chip-to-chip interfaces — tighter tolerances than standard semiconductor packaging. AMKR and ASX (ASE Group) provide OSAT services for photonic ICs. KLIC (Kulicke & Soffa) provides die bonding equipment for photonic module assembly. Shibuya Corp provides specialized bonding systems. Test: TER (Teradyne) and KEYS (Keysight) supply optical signal analyzers and BER testers for 800G/1.6T validation. FORM (FormFactor) provides probe cards for photonic IC wafer-level testing. ATEYY (Advantest) covers high-speed digital test for optical driver ICs.

spine_switching.label: AI Cluster Spine Switching
spine_switching.thesis: Arista's 400G/800G Ethernet switches are the spine fabric for every major AI training cluster. The architecture is non-negotiable: NVDA GPU racks connect to each other via high-radix 800G switches — Arista's 7800R series is the de facto standard for hyperscaler AI build-out. eos_software.label: EOS Network Operating System
eos_software.thesis: Extensible Operating System (EOS) is the recurring revenue moat. Software/services revenue is growing faster than hardware — improving margin profile. This is the Koss 'moat' layer: switching costs are multi-year, non-price-sensitive. leaf_switching.label: ToR / Leaf Switching (derivative)
leaf_switching.thesis: Top-of-Rack (ToR) and leaf switching is more competitive — Cisco, Nokia, and white-box alternatives compete. ANET participates here but this layer is commoditizing. NVDA GPU revenue leads the entire chain (GPUs ordered 9-12 months ahead), but ANET follows within 1-2Q.
